hero.title: First steps to better posture
hero.sub: 3 lessons you can repeat at home.

audience.label: who it's for
audience.lead: Whether you have worked on your posture before or are just starting, this programme will help most if:
items: You don't like how your body looks: slouching, rounded shoulders, a belly that sticks out
You have pain or tension in your back, neck, lower back or between the shoulder blades
You feel you don't really understand or sense your own body
You lack confidence and want to feel freer and more comfortable in your body
You don't know which exercises suit you and doubt whether you're doing them right
You've tried before, but without a clear plan you quickly lost motivation and stopped
audience.outro: If you recognise yourself in even one of these, this programme is for you.

lessons.label: what's inside
lessons.lead: 3 foundational lessons. Each one builds on the one before.

items.title: Hip and rib cage mobility
body: Hip mobility is the basis of posture work. It supports the pelvic area and eases pain and stiffness in the lower back.
Rib cage mobility helps if you feel tightness or stiffness in your upper back, back and neck. Breathing and movement both become freer.

items.title: Basic self-correction
body: "How do I straighten up properly?" is one of the questions I hear most often. The answer is the skill of basic self-correction.
This is the tool that lets you see yourself standing straight in the mirror, with a straight back and an engaged core. And you will feel relief in your body.
details: When we exercise — posture work, the gym, yoga, any sport — while keeping our usual imbalances and poor alignment, we risk locking those patterns in even deeper.
If the foundation, our posture, is built wrong, exercise may not only fail to give the result you want but can make existing problems worse.
That is why moving into self-correction is the first step before any load.

items.title: Holding self-correction under load
body: The final piece: we turn the straight posture you built in lesson two into a natural habit.
Learning to straighten up consciously is great. But for that position to become natural for your body, it has to be reinforced. That is exactly what we do in lesson three.

lessons.outro: Once you finish all 3 lessons, you'll see for yourself: healthy posture is simpler than it seems.

items.a: The lessons are recorded in Russian. [English subtitles — to be confirmed.]

items.q: How long do the lessons take?
items.a: About 50 minutes in total. They are recorded in a follow-along format, so you can do them whenever suits you.

2–3 kg dumbbells and 2 sticks at shoulder height or taller (mops, brooms, ski poles) are a nice bonus, but not required. Swap the dumbbells for something heavy, like 2 bags of sugar or 2 water bottles. Swap the sticks for chair legs, or do without: they only help you find support and your centre of gravity.
I explain every exercise in as much detail as possible: what to do, how, and where you should feel it.

items.q: Will the lessons help with pain?
items.a: Many people feel better, but the lessons don't replace a doctor. If your pain is acute or unexplained, see a specialist first.
